newsitem.title: UK: INDEPENDENT INS CONFIDENT ABOUT PROSPECTS.
newsitem.headline: INDEPENDENT INS CONFIDENT ABOUT PROSPECTS.

text.p: Britain's Independent Insurance on Wednesday reported a 20 percent rise in pretax profits for the first half helped by a strong performance by the UK commercial account.
Profits rose to 20 million pounds ($31.6 million) for the period, excluding realised investment gains of 5.9 million pounds.
Chief executive Michael Bright described the performance as "encouraging" despite tough competition in the UK insurance market and he said the group viewed the future with great confidence.
However, he said he did not expect any significant upturn in the UK market until late 1998 and new participants continued to enter every part of the company's business.
Reported gross written premiums rose 16 percent to 269.9 million pounds but due to the long-term policy arrangements now offered by the group, the underlying position was flat.
The interim dividend was raised 18 percent to 6.25 pence per share.
